newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Dostum's stronghold tense but quiet -Russian consul.
newsitem.headline: Dostum's stronghold tense but quiet -Russian consul.

text.p: The Russian consul in Mazar-i-Sharif, stronghold of opposition leader General Abdul Rashid Dostum, said the situation in the northern Afghan city was tense but quiet on Tuesday, Itar-Tass news agency reported.

It quoted Nikolai Shevchenko as saying public services and shops were open as usual despite reports Dostum commander General Abdul Malik had switched sides and launched a pro-Taleban revolt in at least four opposition-held provinces.
"After the mutiny started checkpoints at the entrances to the city have been reinforced and security measures have been stepped up," Shevchenko told Tass in a telephone interview.
He said at least some of the reports about the success of the mutiny backed by the Islamic Taleban government, which controls two thirds of Afghanistan including the capital Kabul, were exaggerated.

"Taleban is waging a powerful propaganda campaign and often falls into wishful thinking," Shevchenko said. "For instance, Taleban reports about unrest or even fighting in Mazar-i-Sharif are pure lies from beginning to end."
Shevchenko said Dostum's forces were confronting Taleban on the border with Faryab province, the stronghold of Malik.
